subject: Redwood SDK Quickstart & Next Steps - TechFin integration
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@techfin.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 17:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SDK Quickstart & Next Steps - TechFin integration

Alex - thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get your engineering team unblocked on the integration:

1) Recap (from our call)
- Primary use: customer support summarization + reranking of candidate answers for prioritization.
- Traffic profile: bursty during business hours, ~10-20 reqs/sec initially with 2-3k tokens per session average.
- Security: TechFin needs SOC 2 evidence and options for VPC/private deployment later.

2) Recommended technical approach (high level)
- Start with the Redwood hosted API for speed of onboarding, using the TypeScript SDK sample app we linked. If you need traffic isolation, we can transition to Dedicated later.
- Auth: API keys for dev/testing; for production we recommend per-service keys + token rotation via your secrets manager (we can share a template).
- Routing: use per-route model pinning and fallback policy (we'll share config).
- Structured output / tool calling: recommend trying function-calling for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows; sample schema included in the quickstart.
- Embeddings & rerankers: pipeline sample uses Redwood embeddings -> vector store (we show a minimal SQLite example for local testing) and a small reranker model for precision.

3) Immediate next steps (action items)
- I: Share the TypeScript sample app and Python quickstart (attached).
- You: Confirm preferred language for the POC (TypeScript/Python).
- Dev: Offer a 45-min follow-up pairing session to walk through env setup and local testing.
- We: Provide a template config (techfin-config-template.yaml) and a short mutual action plan.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (quickstart + sample snippets). Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart

Can you confirm that TypeScript is the preferred stack and whether your SRE team wants to join the follow-up? I can propose times for a pairing session tomorrow/Thursday.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0114

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@techfin.io>

Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SDK Quickstart & Next Steps - TechFin integration

Thanks Marissa - great session. TypeScript is our preference for the POC (Node service that will call the SDK). A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Local testing: can you confirm the minimum environment we need to run the TypeScript sample locally (Node version, env vars, expected memory)?
- Embeddings: we want to store vectors in an internal vector store (we use Pinecone for now). Does the sample support outputting embeddings only (no generation) so we can pipeline into our existing store?
- Security: our security lead asked for SOC 2 evidence and any docs about network isolation for Dedicated/Private options. Can you share the SOC 2 attestation and a short note about VPC options?

Sofia and I will loop in our SRE if needed - can you include a few times for the follow-up pairing?

Best,
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, TechFin
alex.johnson@techfin.io

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@techfin.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 20:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SDK Quickstart & Next Steps - TechFin integration

Alex - happy to jump in. Quick answers and proposal:

- Local env: Node 18+, yarn 1.x or npm 8+, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your environment. The sample app uses a lightweight in-memory vector store for demos; we've added a Pinecone adapter in the repo (see /adapters/pinecone).
- Embeddings-only: yes - the SDK supports embeddings() as a standalone call; you can push vectors directly to your store. We'll include a minimal script in the sample app for that path.
- Memory: Dev machine with 8GB RAM is sufficient for local dev; Docker image for the sample is ~600MB.
- SOC2 / VPC: attaching the SOC2 overview is on Marissa's side (she'll share). For Dedicated/Private we support VPC peering and customer-managed network paths; I'll attach a config template you can start with.

I can host the 45-min pairing session tomorrow (Wed) 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 9:00-11:00 PT. If those don't work, propose a slot and I will confirm.

Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart/tree/main/sample-apps/ts-chat
Drive (configs): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cTechFinShared

—Dev
